question.text: Under SCRR Rule 15(1), which books of accounts must stock exchange members maintain for 5 years?

answer.text: Register of transactions (Sauda book), clients' ledger, general ledger, journals, cashbook, bank pass-book, and documents register
Only the clients' ledger and general ledger
Only the cashbook and bank pass-book

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 15(1) requires 5-year preservation of: Register of transactions (Sauda book), Clients' ledger, General ledger, Journals, Cashbook, Bank pass-book, and Documents register showing full particulars of shares and securities received and delivered. The Trap: All seven types of books fall under the 5-year requirement. Narrower options that pick only one or two books understate the rule. Note: Rule 15(2) covers a separate 2-year preservation set including contract books, counterfoils of contract notes, and written consent of clients for contracts entered into as principals. The full Rule 15(2) list — not just contract books and counterfoils — is the source-accurate contrast.
